title: Saving, Spending, Borrowing and Producers

key_big: Saving adds up; deposits go in, withdrawals come out.
key_sub: Producers make things; consumers buy them.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Saving means keeping money for later instead of spending it. Small amounts add up over time.
  • A deposit puts money into an account; a withdrawal takes money out.
  • A lender gives something to borrow; a borrower uses it and gives it back. Responsible borrowers return things on time.
  • Producers make goods; consumers buy and use them.

Examples

Example

Save $3 a week for 5 weeks

$3 + $3 + $3 + $3 + $3

Answer: $15

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the saving only onceAdd it for every week.
Mixing up deposits and withdrawalsDeposit = in. Withdrawal = out.
Mixing up producers and consumersProducers make; consumers buy.

items.q: Who is the borrower? A bank lends money to Mr. Diaz to buy a truck.
items.e: The one who gets the loan is the borrower: Mr. Diaz.

items.q: Which is an example of a lender?

items.q: Who is the lender? Ana lends Ben her pencil.
items.e: The person who gives something to borrow is the lender: Ana.

items.q: Which is an example of borrowing?

items.e: Using something that belongs to someone else, then returning it, is borrowing.
